title: REPL Codelab: Threaded Onramp Journey (notes, flows, sample kit)
body:
Purpose:
Create a bite-sized interactive onboarding path that teaches devs how to iterate with the Redwood SDK using a REPL-first experience. This doc captures an experimental codelab design (threaded steps + progressive samples) we can prototype during the sprint.

Audience:
- New SDK adopters who want rapid feedback loops (30–60 minutes)
- Engineers evaluating latency/cost tradeoffs with small workloads
- Developer advocates running workshops or office hours

High-level idea:
- Start with a small, isolated sandbox environment (browser-based REPL + ephemeral token) that 1) shows API calls, 2) live-streams responses, 3) exposes simple telemetry (latency, token cost).
- Structure as "threads": each thread focuses on a single concept (auth, streaming, caching, fallbacks, batching). Threads are short (3–5 steps) and end with a tiny exercise.
- Provide downloadable "sample kits": node/py/minimal containers that reproduce the REPL flows locally.

Core flows (thread list):
1) Quick Start (3 steps) — get an ephemeral token, make a simple generate() call, inspect response stream.
2) Prompt + Tooling (4 steps) — add a tool call (web-search stub), see structured output and function call flow.
3) Cost & Latency (4 steps) — enable a token meter, compare session with/without batching, quick experiments toggling batch window.
4) Cache & Reuse (3 steps) — prefix caching demo, show how repeated prompts avoid token charges.
5) Resilience & Fallbacks (3 steps) — force a transient error and show automatic model routing + fallback to smaller model.
6) Embeddings mini (3 steps) — generate embeddings for a small doc, do a k-NN retrieval and re-query.

Step structure (example thread: Quick Start):
- Step 0: One-liner objective and expected time (e.g., "Objective: call Redwood -> produce text. Time: 6 min").
- Step 1: Create ephemeral token (button in UI, CLI method). Show token scope and TTL.
- Step 2: Run a sample request in REPL (pre-filled). Watch stream and inspect headers for latency.
- Step 3: Tiny challenge: change temperature to 0 and see deterministic result. Commit changes to the sample kit.

Sandbox UX notes (quick brain dump):
- REPL should show request/response and a side-panel with: tokens consumed, approximate cost, latency histogram (30s window), model used.
- Provide a "dumb mode" toggle with simpler UI for non-technical attendees.
- Allow copying sample code to clipboard in 3 languages (js/py/curl).
- Ephemeral token creation should create a disposable workspace that expires in 24 hours.
- Telemetry capture: minimal required events (sample-run, step-complete, error, toggle-batching).

Sample kit (files to include):
- README.md (目的, quick steps)
- sample.js (node, uses SDK with streaming example)
- sample.py (python, same flow)
- Dockerfile (for local containerized run)
- data/ (small text corpus for embeddings thread)
- tests/ (smoke tests: make a call, check status)

Telemetry & gating:
- Define 6 telemetry events we can rely on in the pilot: codelab_start, step_complete, sample_run, sample_error, kit_download, workshop_completion.
- Store minimal pii-free payload (user-id hash, step-id, duration, model_name).
- Gate the first pilot on privacy review (Security sign-off) since ephemeral tokens touch provisioning APIs (ticket: SEC-210).

Accessibility & localization: brief notes
- All text should be localizable; keep strings external in README and UI.
- Design REPL with keyboard-first controls and sufficient color contrast.

Developer advocate / workshop flow (30m exercise plan):
- 0–5 min: intro to Redwood API and goals
- 5–15 min: run Quick Start + Prompt tooling thread (paired)
- 15–22 min: cost/latency thread (show batching toggle)
- 22–28 min: embeddings mini + retrieval example
- 28–30 min: wrap + ask participants to file feedback via small form.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How many ephemeral sessions can we provision per account without rate limiting? (ask infra: @evan)

Notes:
- Quick experimental constraint: keep initial codelab dependency-free (no external DBs) — use in-memory retrieval for embeddings thread.
- Keep all sample code under permissive license (MIT).
- Record a 6-minute walkthrough video after prototype is stable.
